note.title: Assessment Practice — listening rehearsal
note.overview: Audio-first listening rehearsal using the verified Year 9 language and grammar scope. The transcript stays hidden until feedback so the learner must listen for meaning.
learningGoals: Identify gist and key detail from short spoken French.
Hear time markers and distinguish past/present/future.
Cope with unfamiliar language without stopping at every word.
mustMemoriseRules: Second listen: time marker, negative, opinion, person or number.
Perfect tense often signals a completed event; imperfect often signals background or habit.
ne…pas / ne…jamais / ne…rien can reverse the apparent meaning.
workedExamples: Audio: « Hier, j'ai visité un musée. » → key detail: a museum, completed past.
Audio: « Quand j'étais plus jeune, je jouais… » → past habit/background: imperfect.
commonMistakes: Trying to translate every word before identifying the gist.
Hearing a familiar verb but ignoring the time marker.
Confusing perfect and imperfect when both refer to the past.
detailedExplanation: This is an app-built listening rehearsal. The skill is verified against the official Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 French curriculum outcome to understand authentic spoken French.
The audio is generated from written French practice sentences within the verified Year 9 scope; it is not a recording from the school and is not presented as an official listening paper.
Replay is allowed in practice mode. The aim is accurate listening strategy before speed.
examTips: Do not look for every word; listen for who, when, what and attitude.
On replay, target the one detail the question asks for.
Negatives and time markers deserve special attention.
quickCheck: Can I notice ne…pas / jamais / rien?
Can I distinguish perfect from imperfect by context?
Can I answer a detail without translating the whole sentence?
beforeStartingPractice: Use headphones if possible. Listen once before replaying.
